pr_title: Add option to remove file from gist
pr_body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!
  To reference an open issue, please write this in your description: `Fixes #NUMBER`
-->

Fixes #7517 

* Add `--remove` flag in `gist edit`
    - to keep it consistent with add file flag
* will throw error if combined with `add` or `filename` flag
* does not support multiple file delete
pr_comments:
> Hi @kousikmitra, thanks a lot for taking on this work. Generally it looks pretty good and achieves the goal of non-interactive deletion of gist files.
> 
> Firstly, I have requested some changes which I hope make sense to you.
> 
> Secondly, in #7517 we also said this should work [interactively](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/7517#issuecomment-1570741605). Is there a reason you left this out? I'd be happy to merge this PR and follow up with the interactive behaviour in another PR but I also want to give you the opportunity to implement it.

Hey @williammartin , I was trying to do the interactive bit. But the problem is I could not find a feature in cobra which supports a flag with optional argument. 

if a flag is defined as `StringVarP` to support `edit --remove filename` the same flag can't be used without a value like `edit --remove`. 
There are some workaround.
1. Make the flag boolean and take the filename as positional argument
2. Set `NoOptDefVal` for the flag, to use this we have to enter the command like this `edit --remove=filename` cause when this field is set it will interpret the filename in command `edit --remove filename` as positional argument

1st option is a bit hacky but won't change how user is interacting with cli, I don't like the 2nd option as it changes the how the flag has to be used.

Let me know if there's an better alternative. I will make the change in this PR only.

Thanks for that information @kousikmitra, I think I got confused with `gh gist edit` offering interactivity with a file picker but it's not a flag, as you call out.

I don't really like either of the options you presented, and I'm not aware of another option but if we discover one later we can always make that change in a non-breaking manner. I'm inclined to say that we leave this feature as non-interactive. It's not ideal but the user is able to find filenames using `gh gist view --files` so it is possible to find the filenames through the CLI and go from there.

> LGTM thank you for your continued contribution! ✨
> 
> Please squash + merge this when you are ready.

Thanks @williammartin Ready from my side.

I don't have write access, someone with write access need to merge. I am hoping manual squash is not needed, let me know if you want me to do that.
Sorry @kousikmitra, I'm new to the team and didn't realise contributors couldn't merge their own PRs after approval. Cheers!

issue_context.title: Delete files in gists
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

Files can't be deleted in gists...

### Proposed solution

Add the `-d` option to `gist edit`.

### Additional context

Interactive if no file is specified?
comments:
Hi @dardo82, thanks for the enhancement request. This sounds like a sensible feature to me except that `gist edit` already has a `-d` flag (so let's just pick `-r / --remove-file` for the moment since that's what it is called in the UI). Let me see if I've got this right:

### Non-interactive mode

```bash
➜  gh gist edit {<id> | <url>} -r my_file.txt
```

### Interactive mode

```bash
➜  gh gist edit {<id> | <url>} -r
? Select a file to delete  [Use arrows to move, type to filter]
> my_file.txt  about 1 minute ago
  option.rb  about 3 months ago
```

Is that what you had in mind?

I'd also love to hear a bit more about your use case, do you usually work with gists from the command line, are you scripting something, etc. Cheers!
Removal is the last one missing from the basic set of operations called CRUD, no?
Yes I think that's true. I'm not sure how it relates to my previous comment though.

How hard will it be to add this option?
I'm OK with your proposed design for it.

From the docs for [updating a gist](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/gists/gists?apiVersion=2022-11-28#update-a-gist):

> The gist files to be updated, renamed, or deleted. Each `key` must match the current filename (including extension) of the targeted gist file. For example: `hello.py`. To delete a file, set the whole file to null. For example: `hello.py : null`.

I think this feature would iterating over the files in the [fetched gist](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/7a814b31c2cb1512d3d93433e510db28d8398a87/pkg/cmd/gist/edit/edit.go#L112), and when the `Filename` matches the provided one, set the value in the [`Files` map](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/7a814b31c2cb1512d3d93433e510db28d8398a87/pkg/cmd/gist/shared/shared.go#L30) with that key to `nil` and then [update the gist](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/7a814b31c2cb1512d3d93433e510db28d8398a87/pkg/cmd/gist/edit/edit.go#L291). So, I think this shouldn't be too hard (but this is the first time I've looked at this code).

I'm inclined to accept this as a reasonable enhancement and mark this as `help wanted` so that someone in the community can pick it up. However, since I'm new to this project, I'm going to tag @vilmibm for his opinions as he has spent more time around the `gist` commands.
This seems reasonable to me! The absence of this feature is an oversight and not intentional.

So the `gh api gist` command can do it?
But `gh gist edit -r` would be simpler.

A couple of further questions we should answer.

### What should happen if you provide the `-r` flag with other flags?

```bash
➜  gh gist edit {<id> | <url>} -r my_file_to_delete.txt -a my_file_to_add.txt
```

Should we treat this as an error or try to handle it? What would we do if this were interactive?

### Should we support deleting multiple files in one command?

```bash
➜  gh gist edit {<id> | <url>} -r file_1.txt -d file_2.txt
```

## Proposal

Given that:
 * `gist edit -a file_1.txt -a file_2.txt` only adds one file (silently ignoring the other, just due to how flag parsing is done)
 * `gh gist edit -f file2.txt -a file3.txt` doesn't respect both flags (-f is silently ignored)

I would be inclined to scope this work to single file deletion, and an explicit error if `-r` is provided with other flags.

@vilmibm for any extra thoughts.
Yeah, be consistent with the design of other options if there aren't specific reasons for it to be different...
I'm +1 on scoping to single file deletion as well as not allowing `-r` with other flags.
As [discussed](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/7560#issuecomment-1603041513), this has been implemented without the interactive flow. Thanks all.

review_comments: Please add tests to ensure mutual exclusivity of the flags.
